(VIII)--(कुशद्वीप, कुमुदद्वीपम्?)--thrice the Suroda in size surrounded by घृतोड (sea of Ghee) (milk ocean-म्।प्।). Its name comes from a shining divine cluster of grass in it. Its king was a son of Priyavrata, हीरण्यरेतस्, who divided it among his seven sons. Here Agni is worshipped.

--capital of आनर्त (कोशल- वा। प्।) kingdom. Comparable once to अमरावती, dis- appeared; and in its place came द्वारका; finding Kakudmi, its king not returning from ब्रह्मलोक, राक्षसस् like पुण्यजनस् entered it and his ९९ brothers fled to different directions in fear, and established small kingdoms there.

(I)--a son of Uparicara and a king of the Cedis. भा. IX. २२. 6.

--a son of कुश and father of गाधि or कौशीक, who was Indra himself who offered to be his son when कुशाम्ब performed austerities to have a child equal to Indra. (कुशाश्व-वा। प्।). भा. IX. १५. 4; Br. III. ६६. ३२; Vi.
--one of the four sons of कुश. वा. ९१. ६२.
(I)--the king who engaged himself in austeri- ties for a son for one thousand years when Indra himself was born his son गाधि by name. See कुसस्तम्ब। Br. III. ६६. ३३. 5.
